intro: String methods wahi roz-marra ka kaam karte hain: input saaf karna, text todna-jodna, dhundna aur validate karna. Sabse bada trap ye hai ki string immutable hai — method naya string return karta hai, original ko chhoota nahi. Isliye 'method chala diya par result store nahi kiya' wala bug beginners ke saath hamesha hota hai, aur isi section me usko hamesha ke liye theek kiya jata hai.
theory: Har string method naya string (ya number/list) return karta hai; original string kabhi nahi badalti. Isliye cleaned = text.strip().lower() likhna padta hai — sirf text.strip() ka result kho jata hai.

Case methods: lower/upper display ke liye, casefold comparison ke liye (Unicode-safe, 'STRASSE'.casefold() == 'strasse'), title/capitalize human display ke liye — aur ye har word ki hyphen/quote boundary par bhi todte hain.

Whitespace aur splitting: strip/lstrip/rstrip optional characters lete hain, split() bina argument kisi bhi whitespace run par todta hai (aur leading/trailing hatata hai), jabki split(',') exact character par todta hai. join() list ko jodta hai — separator 'sep'.join(parts).

Search aur replace: find() -1 deta hai, index() ValueError deta hai; startswith/endswith tuples accept karte hain (multiple suffixes), replace() ek count limit leta hai, removeprefix/removesuffix (3.9+) prefix/suffix ke liye safer aur explicit hain.

Validation: isalpha/isdigit/isalnum/isspace/isnumeric/isupper/islower. Ye Unicode-aware hain — '१२'.isdigit() True ho sakta hai. Translation ke liye str.maketrans + translate, aur formatting ke liye format/format_map.

s.split(); s.split(',', 1); s.rsplit(',', 1)

s.startswith(('http://', 'https://')); s.endswith('.csv')

s.isalpha(); s.isdigit(); s.isspace(); s.isidentifier()
str.maketrans({'a': '4', 'e': '3'}); s.translate(table)
f'{name}'.strip(); '{:.2f}'.format(value); '{name}'.format_map(row)

s.zfill(8); s.center(20, '-'); s.ljust(10); s.rjust(10)
s.splitlines(); s.splitlines(keepends=True)
s.encode('utf-8'); b.decode('utf-8')

split() bina argument kisi bhi whitespace par todta hai, isliye double space bhi ek hi separator maana jata hai (split(' ') aisa nahi karta).

find() position deta hai, count() ginti — replace() ka count argument sirf pehli n occurrences badalta hai.

examples.code:
TEXT = '''Python   string methods
many kaam karte hain!!  

Clean karna zaroori hai.'''

def normalize(text):
    lines = [line.strip() for line in text.splitlines()]
    lines = [line for line in lines if line]
    return ' '.join(lines)

def collapse_spaces(text):
    return ' '.join(text.split())

clean = collapse_spaces(normalize(TEXT))
print(repr(clean))
print('words:', len(clean.split()))

stripped = clean.lower().strip('!. ')
print('stripped punctuation:', repr(stripped[-30:]))

table = str.maketrans({'a': '4', 'e': '3', 'i': '1', 'o': '0'})
print('leet:', clean[:28].translate(table))

print('title :', clean.title()[:34])
print('center:', '[{}]'.format(clean[:10].center(16, '=')))
print('checks:', clean[:5].isalpha(), clean[:5].istitle(), repr(clean[:5].zfill(8)))
explain: splitlines() newline types (\n, \r\n) dono handle karta hai — isliye file text clean karne me splitlines safer hai.
collapse: text.split() saare whitespace runs ko todta hai aur ' '.join se single spaces aate hain — double space aur tabs ek saath normalize ho jate hain.
translate + maketrans character-level replacement ka fast tarika hai (chain of replace() se behtar), aur strip('!. ') strip ko char-set treat karta hai, prefix nahi.

realWorld: Form aur CSV cleaning: user ka ' Pune ' aur 'pune' ek hi city hai — strip + casefold + punctuation remove ka order har data pipeline ka pehla step hota hai, warna group-by me do rows ban jati hain.
Log parsing: find/index se message nikalna, count se error tally, aur replace se masking (credit card digits, email) — security logs me PII redaction isi tarah hota hai.
Filename aur URL handling: removesuffix/removeprefix aur endswith tuple validation se extension-based routing (upload API me .csv/.json) safe rehta hai — bina regex ke.

interview.q: strip() aur replace() ne string badla nahi — kaise?
interview.a: Strings immutable hain: ye methods naya object return karte hain aur original waisa hi rehta hai. Isliye s.strip() ka result store karna padta hai. Performance-wise in-place feel deta hai kyunki Python internally join/replace ko optimized C me karta hai, par semantics copy-based hai.
interview.tip: Interview me immutability ka practical asar (hashability, thread safety, memory) bhi mention karo.

interview.q: split() aur split(' ') me difference kya hai?
interview.a: split() whitespace ka koi bhi run separator maanta hai aur leading/trailing whitespace hata deta hai — is liye 'a  b'.split() -> ['a', 'b']. split(' ') exact single space par todta hai, isliye 'a  b'.split(' ')-> ['a', '', 'b'] (empty string aa jati hai). CSV/TSV me exact separator chahiye, human text me split() better hai.
interview.tip: Ye interview me favor ka question hai — ek line ka example do, bas.

interview.q: Text comparison ke liye lower() ya casefold()?
interview.a: casefold() — ye Unicode ke liye aggressive normalize karta hai (ß -> ss), isliye case-insensitive comparison correct hoti hai. lower() sirf character-wise lowercasing karta hai aur kuch scripts me 'equal hone chahiye' wale cases miss kar deta hai. Display ke liye lower()/title() theek hai, comparison ke liye casefold().
interview.tip: Turkish 'I'/dotless-i case bhi batao — locale-aware comparison ka nuance dikhata hai.

interview.q: find() vs index() vs in — kab kaun?
interview.a: Sirf 'mojood hai ya nahi' puchna ho to 'sub in s' (fast, readable). Position chahiye par missing case normal hai to find() (-1). Missing case exception hona chahiye to index(). Repeated search ya multiple patterns ke liye re module better hai — 1000 calls se pehle regex consider karo.
interview.tip: Exception-driven flow vs sentinel return ka trade-off discuss karo — interviewer design sense dekhta hai.

interview.q: Ek bada log text se saare URLs nikalne hain — string methods kaafi hain?
interview.a: Nahi. String methods substring ke liye hain, pattern ke liye nahi. URL/email jaise structured patterns ke liye re (regex) use karo: re.findall(r'https?://[^\s]+', text). String methods tab best hain jab delimiter fix ho (split, partition, startswith/endswith).
interview.tip: Regex ka answer dene ke baad ek simple case bhi batao jahan string method better hai — balanced judgement dikhata hai.

beginner.q: '  Pune  ' ko saaf karke title case me print karo.
beginner.explain: strip pehle (warna title extra spaces par bhi kaam karega) aur title display ke liye.
beginner.tip: title() har word capitalize karta hai, capitalize() sirf pehla — farak naam ke saath samjhao.

beginner.explain: split() words deta hai (extra spaces bhi handle), join list ko string me badalta hai — ye dono ka jodi hamesha use hoti hai.

beginner.q: Check karo ki string sirf digits hai, sirf letters hai, ya mixed.
beginner.a: s.isdigit(), s.isalpha(), s.isalnum() — mixed ke liye isalnum True par isdigit/isalpha False.

beginner.tip: Numeric validation ke liye int() try karna zyada reliable hai — isnumeric() float ('١.٥') ke liye bhi True de sakta hai.

beginner.explain: replace() galat jagah bhi kaam kar jata hai (e.g. 'report.csv.csv' yaa middle me), removeprefix/suffix sirf boundary par.

intermediate.explain: Regex se pehle structural checks se 90% garbage nikal jata hai aur error message user-friendly banta hai.
intermediate.tip: Production me full validation ke liye email-validator ya regex + MX lookup hota hai — ye answer mention karo.

intermediate.a: casefold, non-alnum ko space me badlo, split, strip, join('-').

advanced.q: Ek redaction function likho jo email aur phone ko mask kare (log safety ke liye).
advanced.a: Pattern-based replace: email ke local part ka pehla character rakho, phone ke aakhri 4 digits rakho.
advanced.explain: Security-safe logging me PII mask karna compliance requirement hoti hai.
advanced.code:
import re

def mask_email(match):
    local, domain = match.group(0).split('@')
    return f'{local[0]}***@{domain}'

def mask_phone(match):
    digits = match.group(0)
    return '*' * (len(digits) - 4) + digits[-4:]

EMAIL = re.compile(r'[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.]+')
PHONE = re.compile(r'\b\d{10}\b')

line = 'user anjali.sharma@example.com called from 9876543210 on 2026-09-24'
redacted = EMAIL.sub(mask_email, line)
redacted = PHONE.sub(mask_phone, redacted)
print(redacted)
print('email still present?', bool(EMAIL.search(redacted)))
print('phone still present?', bool(PHONE.search(redacted)))
advanced.tip: Interview me 'regex ke bina kya karoge' poochha ja sakta hai — split/partition se partial masking ka tarika bhi sochо.

advanced.q: Do texts ki similarity nikaalo (Jaccard) string methods se, aur sabse common shabd batao.
advanced.a: Donon ko normalize karke word sets banao; jaccard = |A∩B| / |A∪B|.
advanced.explain: Preprocessing (normalize) ke bina similarity galat aati hai — yahi NLP ka pehla lesson hai.
advanced.tip: Bade texts me shingling/tf-idf better hai — Jaccard short texts ke liye theek hai, ye limitation batao.

advanced.q: Ek 'smart title' function likho: chhote words (a, an, the, of) ko capitalize na kare, pehla/aakhri word hamesha capitalize ho.
advanced.a: Words ko casefold karo, position dekhkar title-case lagao, aur minor words ko skip karo (boundary chhodkar).
advanced.explain: title() ka naive behaviour (the -> The) publishing/docs me galat lagta hai — ye real-world polishing task hai.
advanced.tip: Hyphenated words aur acronyms (AI, API) ke liye exception list rakho — production me config se aata hai.

interview.q: Ek 50 MB log file se saari unique error types nikalni hain — approach kya hogi?
interview.a: Line-by-line stream karo (file ko memory me na padho), severity partition se nikalo, set me unique collect karo — memory sirf unique types par. I/O bound hai isliye chunking aur buffered reads use karo.
interview.explain: Large-file handling me streaming aur memory discipline ka jawab chahiye hota hai.

interview.q: String methods se aisa operation karo jo regex se aasan tha — kya limitations hain?
interview.a: String methods fixed substrings, delimiters aur boundary checks ke liye best hain (fast, readable, escape-free). Limitations: repeated patterns, optional groups, lookarounds, captures, aur greedy/lazy matching — in sab ke liye re chahiye. Thumb rule: agar query ko 'plain example' me keh sakte ho to method; agar 'rule/pattern' hai to regex.
interview.explain: Interviewer tool-choice ka judgement test kar raha hai, sirf syntax nahi.

print('methods :', [p.split('-')[1] for p in text.split(', ') if p.startswith('order-')])

interview.q: Ek input field se number lena hai jisme comma aur spaces ho sakte hain — parsing approach batao.
interview.a: Normalize pehle: strip, non-breaking space hatana, thousands comma hatana, aur last comma ko decimal separator maan lena sirf tab jab locale waisa ho. Phir float/Decimal parse, aur invalid par clear error. Ambiguity ('1,234') ko locale ke saath document karo — guess mat karo.
interview.explain: Ambiguous input par guess karna silently galat number deta hai — isliye explicit rule chahiye.
interview.tip: Money ke liye Decimal mention karo — float parse karke paise handle karna bug hai.

realworld.q: User-submitted tags ko normalize karo: lowercase, spaces hatana, khaali tags hatao, duplicates remove karo (order preserve).
realworld.a: casefold + strip per tag, empty filter, aur dict/set-based de-dup with insertion order.
realworld.explain: Tag normalization se search aur analytics consistent ho jate hain.
realworld.code:
raw_tags = '  Python , Data Science ,python,  ML  , , DATA SCIENCE  '

def normalize_tags(raw, sep=','):
    seen, out = set(), []
    for tag in raw.split(sep):
        clean = ' '.join(tag.casefold().split())
        if not clean or clean in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(clean)
        out.append(clean)
    return out

print(normalize_tags(raw_tags))
print('count:', len(normalize_tags(raw_tags)))
realworld.tip: ' '.join(x.split()) whitespace-collapse ka idiom hai — yaad rakho.

realworld.q: Ek uploaded file ke extension se route karo, aur galat extension par friendly error do.
realworld.a: endswith tuple se allowed list check karo; error me allowed formats aur mila hua extension dono likho.
realworld.explain: File handling ka pehla security step hai extension whitelist (blacklist kabhi kaafi nahi hoti).
realworld.tip: Security note: extension par bharosa mat karo — MIME/magic bytes bhi check karo (python-magic).

realworld.q: Ek template renderer banao jo '{name} ne {count} tasks kiye' ko values se bhare, missing key par error de.
realworld.a: str.format_map + custom dict subclass jo missing key par KeyError ke saath available keys bataye.
realworld.explain: format_map me missing-key error ko actionable banana production template systems ki basic requirement hai.
realworld.tip: User-controlled templates ko sandbox karo (attribute access '{a.__class__}' leak karta hai) — security point.

coding.question: Text cleaner likho: input ka extra whitespace, mixed case aur punctuation hatao, phir words ki list return karo.
coding.build: clean_words(text) -> list of lowercase words without punctuation.
coding.input: '  Python   STRING methods!!  Text clean karna aasan hai.  '
coding.hint: casefold pehle, phir strip punctuation per word, aur ' '.join(x.split()) se collapse karo.
coding.concept: split/join, strip with char set, casefold
coding.solution:
import string

PUNCT = string.punctuation

def clean_words(text):
    words = []
    for raw in text.split():
        word = raw.strip(PUNCT).casefold()
        if word:
            words.append(word)
    return words

text = '  Python   STRING methods!!  Text clean karna aasan hai.  '
cleaned = clean_words(text)
print(cleaned)
print('count:', len(cleaned))
print('unique:', len(set(cleaned)))
print('collapsed repr:', repr(' '.join(cleaned)))
coding.explanation: split() pehle whitespace runs ko todta hai (isliye multiple spaces ka issue khatam), phir strip(PUNCT) har word ke dono kinaron se punctuation hatata hai — beech ka punctuation (data-set) safe rehta hai. casefold comparison aur storage ke liye lower() se better hai.
coding.better: Bade documents me generator banao (yield words) taaki list materialize na ho; Unicode normalization (unicodedata.normalize) add karo.
coding.followUp: Hyphenated words ('state-of-the-art') ko ek word rakhoge ya todoge — aur ye decision downstream search ko kaise affect karta hai?

coding.question: Ek 'keyword search' function likho jo text me query ke saare occurrences position ke saath de, case-insensitive.
coding.build: find_all(text, query) -> list of (start, end, snippet)
coding.expected: Har occurrence ki index aur 20-char snippet.
coding.hint: Dono ko casefold karo (length same rehta hai lowercase me) aur find() ko loop me start se aage badhao.
coding.solution:
def find_all(text, query, context=12):
    haystack = text.casefold()
    needle = query.casefold()
    if not needle:
        return []
    hits, start = [], haystack.find(needle)
    while start != -1:
        end = start + len(needle)
        snippet = text[max(0, start - context): end + context].replace(chr(10), ' ')
        hits.append((start, end, snippet))
        start = haystack.find(needle, end)
    return hits

text = 'Data science me data cleaning zaroori hai. Data ka analysis baad me hota hai.'
for start, end, snippet in find_all(text, 'DATA'):
    print(f'{start:>3}-{end:<3} ...{snippet}...')
print('total hits:', len(find_all(text, 'data')))
print('empty query:', find_all(text, ''))
coding.explanation: start = end se aage badhna overlapping hits ko rok deta hai aur infinite loop bhi (query 'aa' ke saath) — ye zaroori safety hai. casefold ke baad index positions original text me hi valid rehte hain (length preservation assumption document karo).
coding.time: O(n × m) worst case (n text, m query) — Python ka find optimized C me hai
coding.better: Bahut bade text ke liye re.finditer ya KMP/Aho-Corasick (multi-pattern) use karo; overlapping matches chahiye to ek-ek index par check karo.
coding.followUp: Multiple keywords (100+) search karne ho to ek-ek find loop kaise slow ho jayega, aur Aho-Corasick ise kaise theek karta hai?

coding.question: Duplicate detector likho jo text me repeated words aur repeated lines dhunde, case-insensitive.
coding.input: Multi-line text with repeated words and one repeated line
coding.expected: Aise words/lines ki list jo ek se zyada baar aayein.
coding.hint: Words ke liye Counter, lines ke liye normalize (strip + casefold) karke Counter.
coding.solution:
from collections import Counter

TEXT = '''Data cleaning is step one.
Python me data cleaning aasan hai.
DATA CLEANING sabse pehla step hai.
'''

def tokens(text):
    return [w.strip('.,!?;:').casefold() for w in text.split() if w.strip('.,!?;:')]

def find_duplicates(text):
    word_counts = Counter(tokens(text))
    line_counts = Counter(' '.join(line.split()).casefold() for line in text.splitlines() if line.strip())
    dup_words = {w: c for w, c in word_counts.items() if c > 1}
    dup_lines = {l: c for l, c in line_counts.items() if c > 1}
    return dup_words, dup_lines

dup_words, dup_lines = find_duplicates(TEXT)
print('duplicate words:', dup_words)
print('duplicate lines:', list(dup_lines)[:2])
print('first line duplicates found:', bool(dup_lines))
print('word count check:', len(tokens(TEXT)))
coding.explanation: Words ke liye punctuation strip + casefold (warna 'Data' aur 'data' alag), lines ke liye whitespace collapse + casefold — dono normalization levels alag hain kyunki comparison unit alag hai.

coding.solution:
from collections import Counter

STOPWORDS = {'is', 'me', 'ka', 'ki', 'hai', 'aur', 'se', 'the', 'a', 'an', 'of', 'to'}

TEXT = '''Python string methods se text clean karna aasan hai!
Data cleaning is the first step of any pipeline.
Methods like strip, split and replace are used the most.'''

def strip_punct(word):
    return word.strip('.,!?;:"()[]')

def preprocess(text, stopwords=STOPWORDS):
    raw_tokens = text.split()
    lowered = [strip_punct(w).casefold() for w in raw_tokens]
    tokens = [w for w in lowered if w]
    kept = [w for w in tokens if w not in stopwords]
    counts = Counter(kept)
    stats = {
        'lines': len(text.splitlines()),
        'raw_tokens': len(raw_tokens),
        'clean_tokens': len(tokens),
        'kept_tokens': len(kept),
        'removed_stopwords': len(tokens) - len(kept),
        'unique': len(counts),
        'avg_token_len': round(sum(len(w) for w in kept) / len(kept), 2) if kept else 0.0,
    }
    return {'tokens': kept, 'top': counts.most_common(5), 'stats': stats}

result = preprocess(TEXT)
for key, value in result['stats'].items():
    print(f'{key:20}: {value}')
print('top terms       :', result['top'])
print('sample tokens   :', result['tokens'][:8])
coding.explanation: Pipeline ke stages explicit hain (lower -> strip -> filter empty -> stopwords) isliye har stage ka count track hota hai — data quality debug karna aasan ho jata hai. stats me avg_token_len aur unique jaisa information rakhna downstream analysis (keyword density) me kaam aata hai.
coding.better: Large corpus ke liye streaming + nltk/spaCy tokenizers, aur stemming/lemmatization add karo; stopword list ko language-specific config se load karo (hardcode na karo).

projects.code:
import string

SAMPLE = '''  Python   STRING methods!!

Text clean karna   aasan hai.  '''

def normalize(text):
    return ' '.join(text.split()).casefold()

def clean_words(text):
    return [w.strip(string.punctuation) for w in normalize(text).split() if w.strip(string.punctuation)]

clean = normalize(SAMPLE)
words = clean_words(SAMPLE)

print('original chars :', len(SAMPLE))
print('clean chars    :', len(clean))
print('clean text     :', repr(clean))
print('words          :', words)
print('word count     :', len(words))
print('unique words   :', len(set(words)))
print('avg word len   :', round(sum(len(w) for w in words) / len(words), 2))
projects.explanation: ' '.join(text.split()) ek line me saare whitespace runs (spaces, tabs, newlines) ko single space me badal deta hai — multi-pass replace se better. clean_words me strip(string.punctuation) kinaron par kaam karta hai, so 'data-set' jaisa internal hyphen bacha rehta hai.

interview.q: Normalization order (collapse, strip, case) ka kya role hai?
interview.a: Pehle whitespace collapse karo (tokens ki boundaries fix), phir per-token strip (punctuation), phir case normalize — agar case pehle karo to koi farak nahi padta par strip/collapse ke baad empty tokens ban sakte hain jo filter karne padte hain. Order document karna zaroori hai taaki tests stable rahein.

interview.q: casefold vs lower is cleaner me kaunsa?
interview.a: casefold — ye Unicode-aware hai aur comparison ke liye aggressive normalize karta hai. lower() display ke liye theek hai par ija comparison me edge cases miss karta hai.

interview.q: Punctuation hatana kab galat decision hai?
interview.a: Jab punctuation meaning badalta ho: 'C++' -> 'c', 'state-of-the-art' -> toota hua word, ya '1,234.50' -> '123450'. Isliye cleanup mode configurable rakho aur domain-specific exceptions (allowed chars) do.

interview.q: Keyword extraction me stop-words hataana hamesha sahi hai?
interview.a: Nahi — 'not', 'no', 'without' jaise negation words hataane se meaning ulta ho jata hai (sentiment/QA me). Domain-specific stopword lists rakho (e.g. search queries me 'the' skip karo, legal text me nahi).

interview.q: Duplicate detection Counter par kyun, difflib par kyun nahi?
interview.a: Exact duplicates ke liye Counter O(n) hai aur simple; difflib near-duplicates ke liye hai par O(n^2) comparisons leta hai. Strategy: Counter se exact dupes nikalo, phir un clusters par difflib chalao (cost kam).

interview.q: Search me casefold ke baad index original text par valid kaise rehta hai?
interview.a: casefold() length badal sakta hai kuch Unicode cases me (ß -> ss), isliye index mismatch ka risk hai. Safe tarika: case-insensitive search ke liye re.IGNORECASE, ya text ko map karke positions track karna. Simple ASCII text me casefold length preserve karta hai — isliye ye assumption document karni chahiye.

interview.q: Inverted index se search fast kaise hota hai?
interview.a: Design time par word -> positions ki mapping ban jati hai, isliye query O(1) average hash lookup hai instead of O(n) scan. Cost: build time O(n) aur memory (positions store karni padti hain). Trade-off: positional index space zyada leta hai, boolean index kam.

Preprocessing ko batch/parallel karo (multiprocessing). Similarity computation ko candidate generation ke saath combine karo (blocking/ANN) warna O(n^2) ho jayega.

revision: Strings immutable hain — har method naya string return karta hai, result store karna zaroori hai.
' '.join(text.split()) whitespace collapse ka idiom hai (saare runs, tabs aur newlines ek saath).
split() vs split(' '): bina argument whitespace runs par todta hai, exact char par split empty strings deta hai.
Comparison ke liye casefold(), display ke liye lower/title/capitalize — inhe mix mat karo.
find() -1 deta hai, index() ValueError; optional substring ke liye partition() sabse safe hai.
removeprefix/removesuffix boundary par kaam karte hain, replace() kahin bhi — extension/filename ke liye prefix/suffix methods better hain.
Validation methods (isalpha/isdigit/isalnum) Unicode-aware hain — numeric parsing ke liye int()/float() try karna zyada reliable hai.
Punctuation strip strip(chars) se karo (char set), multi-pass replace se whitespace collapse never reliable.
Large text ke liye streaming (line-by-line) karo; search ke liye regex aur indexing (inverted index) socho.
